about: The coverage each assembly reaches, held in both directions. A score under its entry is a suite that weakened; a score over its entry is an entry that has stopped describing the tree it sits in, and both are refused. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below and write the percentage the check prints for that assembly. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent, and since #188 a floor left under the measured score reds it too, so the sentence is now held rather than only written. Do not round the report's rate attribute down by hand. A rate is written to at most four decimal places and the attribute carries the float form of that value, so 0.9583 is stored as 0.9582999999999999, and rounding those digits down records a hundredth less than the suite reaches. That is where two of the four entries below sat until this file was corrected. The printed percentage is the same rate multiplied by a hundred and rounded to two decimals, which moves nothing while the report keeps to four, and the check compares the rate itself with a billionth of a point of slack for the float form, so a floor taken off the printed row compares equal rather than above. A collector that starts writing a fifth decimal would break that, and the repair then is to read the rate rather than the row.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: Every partially covered branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. Plugin.cs, PluginServiceRegistrator, RuleDocumentLoader, LibraryChangeSubscription, LibraryChangeCoalescer and LibraryManagerChangeSource all report branch-rate 1 over the branches they declare, the loader's own id-collision arm included: both directions of it are reached, by a directory holding two documents that claim one id and by one holding two that do not. The report puts what is unexecuted on one line, RuleDocumentStore.cs:128 at condition-coverage 83.33% (10/12), which is the six-clause name check that refuses a name composing into a path outside the store's directory. It short-circuits on the first clause that matches, so a name refused by an early clause never reaches the later ones and no set of inputs lights every slot. The coalescer's three defensive arms are inside that branch-rate 1 rather than outside it, and reaching them is why the suite's fake clock can move without running a timer and can run a timer that is not due: a timer is a request and not a promise, so a callback that arrives early, arrives late or arrives with nothing to do is an ordinary input rather than an impossible one.

THE BRANCH FLOOR WAS RAISED HERE RATHER THAN IN THE CHANGE THAT RAISED THE COVERAGE, which is the one thing the note above asks for and the reason this paragraph is longer than the others. 78d0491cf3cfab8ed7ab5c1c478462c34530d394 carried a rule's declared name onto the collection it owns and left this entry at 98.95: its rename arm adds four branch slots to CollectionResolver.ResolveAsync and a test reaches every one, so the assembly moved from 190 of 192 covered slots to 194 of 196, and the rate the report writes moved from 0.9895 to 0.9897. Counted off the condition-coverage attributes of the same reports the rates are read from, at that commit and at its parent e3a1d95e48d1d0fa171aed59bcec3026ef33d710. The line rate does not move with it, because 624 of 626 and 638 of 640 both truncate to 0.9968, and the collector truncates rather than rounds. WHAT THE STALE FLOOR DID NOT DO IS ABSORB A STEP OF WEAKENING, and reading it the other way is the mistake the same correction had to make once already for a hundredth: one branch slot out of 196 is 0.51 points, so a change that stops reaching one lands under 98.95 as surely as under 98.97. The two hundredths are precision in what this file records rather than protection it was missing, and what the gap does cost is a reader who takes an entry for a measurement of the tree it sits in. NOTHING IN THE TREE NOTICED A FLOOR LEFT BEHIND UNTIL #188, AND THIS SENTENCE SAID THE DIRECTION WAS UNBUILT. The check compared the score against the floor and never the floor against the score it was taken from, so this entry stayed green for five merges while it named a figure the suite had passed. It is refused now: the same arm that refuses a score under its floor refuses a score over it, and the message names the assembly, both figures and this file. What has not changed is the reading beside it - the gap absorbed no weakening, and one branch slot out of 196 is 0.51 points either way. Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.branchNote: The only partially covered branch point in the assembly is still the discard in the value-kind description in RuleDocumentValidator, reported at condition-coverage 87.5% (7/8). The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number is not recorded here any more: it moves whenever anything is added above it in that file, and it has moved twice for that reason without the arm itself changing. Read it off the report rather than from this note. The second describer beside it, added with the name member, has both arms reached and adds no partial point, and the id member's own refusals add none either: every arm of the set check, the length check and the two kind checks is reached by a test. The value types add no partial point either. Every arm of every reader is reached: each type has a test accepting its form and a test refusing the value the neighbouring type would accept, the duration walk is reached at each of its refusals including the years-and-months arm and the overflow, and both arms of the bound that cuts a quoted value are reached, by a value at the bound and by one whose cut would otherwise land inside a surrogate pair. The operator table adds no partial point either. Both arms of the acceptance walk are reached, by a pair the table accepts and by one it does not; both arms of the value-type refusal are reached, by an operator that takes a value and by one that takes none; and the two arms that throw rather than answer, an operator with no row and a refusal asked for a pair the table accepts, are each reached by a test. The composition stage adds no partial point either. Every refusal in the walk is reached by a document written to trip it, both directions of the group-count check are reached by an object carrying one member and by one carrying two, the depth arm is reached at the deepest allowed level and one past it, and the member walk is reached by a condition, by a nested group and by a member that is not an object. The field vocabulary adds no partial point either. Both arms of the row walk in the table are reached, by a field that has a row and by one that does not; both arms of the name lookup are reached, by a declared name and by a name differing from one only by case; and every arm of the stage that reads a condition's field is reached, by a condition naming a declared field, by one carrying no field member, by one whose field is not a string, by one naming a field the table does not declare and by a nested group holding each of those. The pointer resolver's arms are reached the same way: an empty pointer, a pointer with no leading slash, an absent member, an index past the end of an array, a token that is not a number, a descent into a value that is neither object nor array, and both escapes in the order the standard decodes them.
